Summarizes the 2002 Spellbound tactics game, its Robin Hood story, five-person mission parties, recruitment, and the money needed to ransom Richard. It also provides links to reviews, platforms, and the developer.

The article describes preserving enemy lives as beneficial to recruitment and lists familiar companions such as Marian, Little John, Will Scarlet, Stuteley, and Friar Tuck.

**Limitations:** this is a secondary overview. Its displayed Mac and Linux release dates differ from PCGamingWiki and RuneSoft, so the dates need edition-specific investigation. Use the bibliography to locate original reporting rather than treating every infobox field as settled.

The article is summarized here in original wording; this entry is not a copy of Wikipedia's text.

_**Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood**_ is a 2002 [stealth-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stealth_game "Stealth game") [real-time tactics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_tactics "Real-time tactics") [video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") developed by [Spellbound Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spellbound_Entertainment "Spellbound Entertainment"). It is similar to games such as _[Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desperados:_Wanted_Dead_or_Alive "Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive")_ and the _[Commandos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commandos_\(series\) "Commandos \(series\)")_ series. In the game, the player controls up to five characters in a setting based on the stories of the protagonist, [Robin Hood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Hood "Robin Hood"). The player can also control Robin Hood's [Merry Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merry_Men "Merry Men"), including [Little John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_John "Little John"), [Friar Tuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friar_Tuck "Friar Tuck"), [Will Scarlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Scarlet "Will Scarlet"), [Will Stutely](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Stutely "Will Stutely"), and [Maid Marian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maid_Marian "Maid Marian"). Robin and his crew must evade the cruel [Sheriff of Nottingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheriff_of_Nottingham "Sheriff of Nottingham") and his henchmen and stop the machinations of the vile usurper to England's throne, [Prince John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John,_King_of_England "John, King of England"). Robin must avoid killing enemies as much as possible, or he will not be able to recruit as many new Merry Men.

## Plot

The game starts with Robin Hood, arriving in [Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln,_Lincolnshire "Lincoln, Lincolnshire") from the [Crusades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crusades "Crusades"), and finding out that his inheritance has been stolen by the notorious Sheriff of [Nottingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nottingham "Nottingham"). After the player finishes the first and second missions, meets [Maid Marian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maid_Marian "Maid Marian") in the Nottingham [cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral "Cathedral"), and subsequently tries to meet the Prince, it is understood that [King Richard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_I_of_England "Richard I of England") has been kidnapped by [Leopold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopold_V,_Duke_of_Austria "Leopold V, Duke of Austria") of [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria "Austria") for a ransom, and that the Regent Prince John is unlawfully usurping the rightful king. The responsibility of getting the ransom of £100,000 to save the king falls into the player's hands. Missions generally include ambushing convoys and infiltrating towns, usually to gather information or even liberate a notable outlaw from the sheriff's clutches. In the final mission, Robin must fight the Sheriff of Nottingham, thereby defeating the Prince.

## Gameplay

While the merry men can kill or wound enemy soldiers, their resources are limited to a certain extent, with main characters having more than minor miscellaneous ones. In addition, in every town, the player can give money to beggars, who, when given coins and purses, help by providing hints and tips. Common folk sometimes, though rarely, offer help but two—a woman in a red apron and a man in a red-and-blue shirt—flee at the sight of a merry man and alert nearby enemy soldiers. The greed of enemy soldiers is also limited, with money purses not affecting sergeants, while [ale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ale "Ale") does affect them. Sometimes, money can be found in [knights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knights "Knights"), cavalry units, sergeants, and more rarely, normal soldiers.

The PC version received "favorable" reviews according to the [review aggregation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"). The Linux version of the game, which was available in German and English, also received favourable mentions.

### Awards

The game received awards for Best Game Design and Best Animation at the 2003 Animago Awards.
